references.text: Jacob mentions Reuben's action as part of his blessing and warning to his sons before his death: Reuben lost his birthright because he went up into his father's bed.
1 Chronicles explicitly explains that Reuben lost his birthright because he defiled his father's marriage bed, and the birthright was given to Joseph's sons.
Absalom lies with David's concubines publicly, a thematic parallel to Reuben's action with his father's concubine Bilhah.
Bilhah was given as a servant woman to Rachel by Laban, providing background on who Bilhah was in Jacob's household.
Paul addresses a man who has his father's wife—a direct parallel to Reuben's sin with his father's concubine—and calls it an immorality not even found among the Gentiles.
Highlights the contrast between Reuben's formal title as firstborn and his actual loss of inheritance rights due to sin.
Connects Reuben's status as firstborn with the consequence of his action (loss of privileges) in later genealogies.
